title: Mahalakshmi to arrive on an elephant this year: 'Puja' to take place under Budhaditya Yog; considered auspi... - Bhaskar English
text:
Diwali 2026: Budhaditya Yog & Mahalakshmi Puja | Auspicious for Business Get the latest news from your city
 Download Sat, Nov 7, 2026 Updated 09:55 AM IST Mahalakshmi to arrive on an elephant this year: 'Puja' to take place under Budhaditya Yog; considered auspicious for trade, business & farmers
 5 hours ago Loading advertisement... 
 To Read Bhaskar English… Better News Experience Read in App In the Browser Continue Diwali will be celebrated on Sunday this year, and Budhaditya Yoga will be formed on the same day. According to astrological beliefs, Goddess Mahalakshmi will arrive riding an elephant this time.
 Loading advertisement... According to Pt. Ajay Krishna Shankar Vyas, an astrologer at Shri Matangi Jyotish Kendra, Diwali falling on a Sunday and the arrival of Goddess Mahalakshmi on an elephant are considered good signs for trade, business and farmers.
 Loading advertisement... Kartik month holds special importance among the 12 months 
 According to astrologer Amar Dibbewala, the five-day Diwali festival began with Kartik Krishna Paksha Ekadashi. Kartik month holds special importance in the Hindu calendar. Several major festivals are celebrated during both the Krishna and Shukla Paksha of this month.
 These include Rama Ekadashi, Govatsa Dwadashi, Dhanteras, Dhanvantari Jayanti, Narak Chaturdashi and Diwali. During the Shukla Paksha, festivals such as Annakut, Bhai Dooj, Saubhagya Panchami, Surya Chhath Puja, Gopashtami, Amla Navami, Dev Prabodhini Ekadashi, Vaikuntha Chaturdashi and Kartik Purnima are celebrated.
 Two festivals falling on the same day 
 According to traditional beliefs, differences between local standard time and Indian Standard Time can sometimes lead to different calculations of festival dates in Indian astrology. This makes it important to clarify the dates of some festivals.
 Dhanteras was celebrated on November 6. The festival of Dhan Trayodashi is linked to the Pradosh period. The Trayodashi date will continue until 10:50 am on November 7, after which Chaturdashi will begin.
 Deep Shraddh ritual observed on Narak Chaturdashi 
 Narak Chaturdashi is observed during the Brahma Muhurta, the early morning period before sunrise. On this day, people perform a ritual called Ulka Daan or Deep Shraddh in memory of their ancestors.
 This is why the festival is considered a morning celebration. The Chaturdashi date will continue until 11:30 am on November 8, after which Amavasya will begin. This means the Amavasya date will remain throughout November 8.
 Owl is the traditional vehicle, elephant symbolises prosperity 
 According to religious beliefs, the owl is the traditional vehicle of Goddess Lakshmi. Some Hindu calendars and astrological beliefs also mention the vehicle on which the goddess arrives on Diwali.
 Owl as the vehicle: The owl is the traditional vehicle of Goddess Lakshmi. It can see even in darkness and symbolises the ability to recognise right and wrong. The belief reminds people not to lose their sense of judgement even after gaining wealth.
 Elephant as the vehicle: The elephant symbolises strength, wealth, prosperity and good fortune. In the Gajalakshmi form of the goddess, elephants are shown performing her ceremonial bathing. This is considered a sign of happiness, peace, wealth, food and prosperity.
